- conditions, exceptions, alternatives, and modality;
- substantive evidence or examples;
- attribution affecting ownership or evidentiary status;
- structural scope needed to understand a component.

Usually omit or compress:

- implied motivation;
- rhetorical emphasis;
- obvious consequences;
- interchangeable illustrations;
- repetitive lists;
- scene-setting without a constraining function;
- citation, numbering, markup, and formatting syntax;
- repetitive entries in a unified component;
- extraction artifacts.

Most items should be one compact sentence and must not exceed 60 words.


# STEP 4 — ASSIGN PRIMARY ROLES

Assign exactly one role to every finalized item.

Choose the role representing the item's primary composition-level or
structural function: the main function that would disappear at that point
if the item were removed.

Determine the role from:

- the item's governing commitment;
- its relationship to preceding and following items;
- the document's overall progression and themes;
- the role definitions;
- the role assignment tests;
- the distinctions among nearby roles.

Do not choose a role based only on:

- keywords;
- topic;
- named entities;
- document position;
- section name;
- formatting or markup;
- the presence of a citation, link, table, figure, heading, note, or
  appendix.

An item may have secondary effects. Ignore them when selecting its single
primary role.

Use the role name exactly as supplied.


## STRUCTURAL ROLE ASSIGNMENT

For an item inside a bounded component, use a substantive or rhetorical
role when its primary commitment is a claim, finding, example, procedure,
interpretation, or other content move.

Use a structural role when its primary commitment is the inclusion and
document-level function of the bounded component itself.

Classify by function rather than container.


## OTHER

Use the reserved role `Other` only when every supplied role would materially
mischaracterize the item's primary function.

Do not use `Other` merely because:

- no role describes every detail;
- a role is broader than the item's specific content;
- the item concerns an unusual topic or entity;
- several roles initially appear plausible;
- the item has secondary effects;
- it occurs in an unusual position or component.

When several named roles are plausible, choose the best-fitting role rather
than `Other`.

Do not change item boundaries to avoid `Other`.

Artifacts must be removed, not labelled `Other`.


# STEP 5 — DESCRIBE THE DOCUMENT TYPE

Write a concise, content-blind description of the specific document type.

Identify when inferable:

- genre or format subtype;
- likely venue or publication setting;
- intended audience;
- communicative register or style;
- broad presentational convention needed to characterize the type.

Do not include topic, themes, named content entities, arguments, findings,
examples, outline structure, human-versus-AI judgments, markup, citation
style, file format, or extraction artifacts.

David Gemmell: Master of Heroic Fantasy
David Andrew Gemmell (1948–2006) was a British author whose name has become synonymous with heroic fantasy. Known for his visceral storytelling, morally complex characters, and unshakable belief in the human spirit, Gemmell’s work redefined the sword-and-sorcery genre. His legacy lives on not only in his novels but in the hearts of countless readers who found strength, hope, and courage within their pages.
Early Life – Forged in Fire: Born on August 1, 1948, in West London, David grew up in a rough, working-class environment. Raised by his mother and his formidable stepfather, Bill Woodford — a former bare-knuckle boxer — David’s early years were marked by street fights, hard lessons, and a deep fascination with heroism. Bill’s quiet strength and stoic sense of right and wrong had a profound impact on the boy, planting the seeds for the kind of characters David would one day write: tough on the outside, deeply moral within. School offered little solace. Expelled as a teenager for organising a gambling synticate, David found himself navigating the margins of society. He took on jobs ranging from labourer to nightclub bouncer, gaining a firsthand understanding of violence, fear, and the importance of having a personal code — all of which would become hallmarks of his writing.
Journalism and the Turning Point: Eventually, David found his way into journalism, working his way up from freelance writing to becoming editor-in-chief of the Hastings Observer. Journalism sharpened his writing and taught him discipline, but fiction was always tugging at the edges of his imagination. In 1976, he faced a personal crisis when doctors suspected he had cancer. Awaiting test results, David began writing a novel as a metaphor for his battle with mortality. That book was The Siege of Dros Delnoch — an epic about a doomed fortress holding out against overwhelming odds, a stand-in for his body fighting against the disease. The book’s central figure, Druss the Legend, was an ageing warrior who embodied the kind of honour, grit, and inner strength Gemmell admired — inspired in part by his stepfather. Druss’s defiant last stand wasn’t just a fantasy tale; it was David’s spiritual rebellion against fear. Fortunately, the diagnosis turned out to be incorrect. However, David shelved the manuscript, believing it to be too personal. But a friend read it and urged him to submit it for publication. In 1984, it was released under a new title: Legend. It would go on to become one of the most influential heroic fantasy novels of the 20th century.
Ross Harding and the Early Non-Fiction Years: Before David became known as a fantasy author, he wrote several works of non-fiction under the pseudonym Ross Harding. These included explorations of social issues and psychology — a reflection of his early interest in people’s motivations and inner lives. Though these works are lesser-known today, they laid the groundwork for the psychological depth and emotional nuance found in his later fiction.
A World of Heroes – Building the Drenai & Beyond: Following the success of Legend, David devoted himself to writing full-time. He went on to create the Drenai Saga, expanding the world of Druss with new characters like the haunted assassin Waylander, the tormented swordsman Skilgannon, and the mixed blood warrior Tenaka Khan. His books often featured recurring themes: the price of redemption, the weight of personal codes, and the struggle between duty and conscience. He also created multiple standalone series and settings, including:
The Rigante Series, blending Celtic myth and political intrigue
The Jon Shannow Trilogy, a post-apocalyptic western with biblical overtones
The Stones of Power series (Sipstrassi Tales), mixing fantasy and alternate history
The Troy Trilogy, his final, historically inspired epic, completed posthumously by his wife Stella Gemmell
Writing Style and Themes: David’s writing style was direct, lean, and emotionally resonant. He favoured tight plotting, action-driven narratives, and deeply personal moral conflicts over elaborate world-building or magic systems. His fantasy was grounded — full of brutal battles, tough choices, and characters who felt unmistakably real. He often said he wasn’t interested in writing about perfect heroes — he wanted to write about flawed people trying to do the right thing. His villains, too, were never one-dimensional; many were men broken by tragedy or corrupted by fear, making their downfall all the more tragic. He also famously reused and reinvented archetypes, creating spiritual successors to characters — such as Druss’s legacy appearing in future generations or parallel timelines. His stories formed a tapestry of struggle, defiance, and hope that spanned time and genre.
Influences: From Middle-earth to Marvel and the Open Range: David’s storytelling roots ran deep, shaped by a diverse range of influences. As a young reader, J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings opened his eyes to the grandeur and mythic scope of fantasy, showing that imaginary worlds could carry profound moral weight. Yet his approach was never purely Tolkienesque — he preferred grit to grandeur, intimacy to sweeping lore. Another major influence was Louis L’Amour, the American author of classic Westerns. L’Amour’s tales of lone gunfighters, rugged landscapes, and ironclad personal codes resonated strongly with Gemmell, who saw parallels between the gunslinger of the frontier and the wandering warrior of heroic fantasy. That sense of stoic honour and self-reliance permeates characters like Waylander and Jon Shannow. And then there was Stan Lee, whose work in Marvel Comics provided a different kind of inspiration. Gemmell admired Lee’s ability to humanise heroes — to give them flaws, doubts, and personal struggles beneath their extraordinary powers. That sensibility echoes throughout Gemmell’s fiction, where even the mightiest warriors wrestle with fear, guilt, and redemption. These three voices — Tolkien’s myth, L’Amour’s grit, and Lee’s flawed humanity — helped shape the foundation of Gemmell’s own brand of heroic fantasy: grounded in realism, charged with moral complexity, and never losing sight of what makes a hero truly human.
Real People in Fictional Armour: Many of David’s characters were inspired by real people in his life. His stepfather was the prototype for Druss. Friends and colleagues often appeared as minor characters or enemies — sometimes at their own request. He believed that the best fiction came from emotional truth, and so his stories were always, at heart, about people. He never lost sight of the fact that fantasy, for all its swords and monsters, was ultimately about what it means to be human.
A Writer for the Readers: David’s connection to his fans and readers was legendary. He answered fan mail personally, attended conventions with humility, and took time to support new writers. He never let fame change him. Despite his growing popularity, he remained grounded, honest, and deeply respectful of his audience. He once remarked that if just one person found strength or comfort in his books, he considered his job done.
Legacy – The Sword That Still Stands: David Gemmell passed away on July 28, 2006, following heart surgery. His death shocked the fantasy world, coming just as he was nearing completion of the final book in the Troy series. His wife Stella, herself an accomplished writer, finished the manuscript so that his last story could be told. In 2009, the David Gemmell Legend Award was established to honour excellence in fantasy fiction and keep his spirit alive in the genre he helped elevate. Though the award ran until 2019, Gemmell’s influence has never dimmed. Today, his novels continue to inspire new generations of writers and readers. His impact on the sword-and-sorcery subgenre is profound: he took pulp fantasy and gave it moral weight, psychological complexity, and emotional resonance. More than a writer of battles, David Gemmell was a writer of bravery — not just the kind found on the battlefield, but the kind it takes to face fear, make hard choices, and keep going.
“What is a hero? Someone who stands when others fall.”
Few writers lived that truth as deeply as David Gemmell.

PhD Candidate at University of Bordeaux in France.
Axel Ransinangue is a Ph.D. candidate at Bordeaux University, conducting research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and geosciences. Specializing in deep learning for carbonate reservoir characterization, his work integrates advanced image processing, computer vision, and geological interpretation. Axel’s expertise spans Python, MATLAB, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and geospatial tools such as QGIS and ArcGIS, enabling him to develop innovative solutions for analyzing thin section images, petrophysical properties, and hyperspectral datasets. Collaborating closely with TotalEnergies, he has designed semi-supervised classification systems, synthetic data generation pipelines, and multiscale segmentation techniques that bridge synthetic and real-world geological imagery. His contributions extend beyond research, actively engaging in scientific communication through conferences and leading discussions in the computer vision community. Driven by a passion for data-driven science, Axel’s work demonstrates both academic rigor and industrial relevance, making him a promising leader in AI-driven geoscience innovation.
Axel holds a Bachelor’s degree in Earth Sciences and Environment with honors from Pau University, where he developed strong foundations in porous media analysis and image processing. He pursued a Master’s degree in Engineering from Bordeaux INP – ENSEGID, graduating with honors, and participated in an international exchange at Kyushu University, Japan, expanding his technical and cultural perspectives. Currently, Axel is a Ph.D. candidate in Artificial Intelligence, Sciences, and Environment at Bordeaux University, working in collaboration with TotalEnergies. His doctoral research integrates AI methodologies with carbonate petrography to enhance reservoir characterization. Under the supervision of experts in geology and computer science, he specializes in representation learning, domain adaptation, and synthetic data conditioning for geological imagery. This interdisciplinary education has equipped him with a unique blend of computational, analytical, and field-specific skills, positioning him at the forefront of AI applications in earth sciences.
Axel’s professional experience blends academic research with industrial applications. At TotalEnergies, as a Geologist Intern, he analyzed carbonate thin sections, interpreting petrographic features for reservoir evaluation. Later, as a Data Scientist at AGEOS, he applied hyperspectral imaging to mineralogical quantification, developing regression models and calibrating point cloud acquisitions. His current role as a Ph.D. researcher involves designing deep learning systems for carbonate reservoir characterization, focusing on semi-supervised classification, conditional synthetic dataset generation, and multiscale image segmentation. He has also explored model explainability, ensuring AI decisions are interpretable for geological experts. Additionally, Axel has worked on integrating bi-modal classification models combining imagery with petrophysical data, as well as anomaly detection frameworks. His cross-domain expertise enables the translation of AI methodologies into practical tools for geoscience, creating value both in research and industrial operations.
Axel’s research lies at the convergence of computer vision, deep learning, and carbonate petrography. His primary objective is to enhance geological image analysis through advanced AI-driven methodologies. Key areas include representation learning with invariance to interpretation biases, synthetic dataset generation conditioned on geological parameters, and domain adaptation to bridge synthetic and real-world imagery. He specializes in texture synthesis, pixel harmonization, and object packing strategies for creating high-quality training data when labeled datasets are scarce. His work also involves developing heuristics-based regularization techniques for improved segmentation accuracy and integrating statistical analysis to link image descriptors with petrophysical properties. By leveraging semi-supervised and multi-modal approaches, Axel aims to create robust and generalizable AI models that address challenges in reservoir characterization. This research not only advances geological sciences but also contributes to broader AI applications in image-based data interpretation across environmental and industrial domains.

Summary: For ECE437: Computer Architecture, my partner Jeremy Tryba and I wrote two fully functional CPUs in VHDL -- multicycle and pipelined -- then tested them in hardware. These projects also gave me some great insights on how to write programs to take into account processor peculiarities. Summary: For this project, we designed and built a 3D Graphics Processing Unit. The unit supported w-buffering, hardware line rasterization, 3D projections, and matrix operations. VESA VBE Banked Mode Library
Summary: A complete programming graphics library that'll do everything you'd ever want, mostly in hand-optimized Intel 386 assembly according to the Video Electronics Standards Association (VESA) Video BIOS Extensions (VBE), which are incidentally still on modern BIOSes (you just can't access them due to WinXP). This implementation was somehow derived straight from the many VESA VBE manuals that VESA produced. Before video cards had enough memory to implement linear framebuffers, they used page buffers where you had to (inconveniently) switch between different video memory pages every 64000 bytes, which could rudely be in the middle of a scan line (note in VGA cards, for example, bit planes even existed which specified one plane per primary color!). We'll just say my library supports this "banked" option because the linear framebuffer implementation is "too easy". Also, interestingly enough, to get around the fact that processors now operated in "protected mode" to get at > 640k of RAM (and thus the BIOS interrupts couldn't be called like in real mode), I had to physically copy the ROM into memory, find the offset of the VESA VBE, then execute that code manually. Interesting way to do it.
Why it's cool: See the summary.
Summary: We used to joke that this game would run on anything, and indeed it does, even today! (Edit: Confirmed it does not run on 64-bit Windows 8!) Why it's cool: Wow, lots of reasons here. My longest program at the time of its writing, In C and graphics in 100% inline assembly. Manually loaded PCX files, had a global 8-bit palette, had the experience of managing a large production team, PC speaker sound effects, mouse assembly routines, high scores, developed my own custom data packing system to pack all assets into one data file. Note that the digits for the points received that float up are actually copied directly from ROM, and they are distorted on modern computers because they changed the character set stored in ROM so that my 1/2 pixel scaling routine doesn't work as well. Also, egad! Windows changed around their color palette system, so unfortunately the black color isn't the same as it used to be, leaving an ugly white mask around every "transparent" object. (So yeah, you got me. I "cheated" ... but I only did it because the assembly code was much easier if I just directly drew the black colors rather than skipping transparent pixels.)
Summary: This is a really short program, but it has an amazing effect -- it generates SIRDS (Single Image Random Dot Stereograms) from 4-bit color images, using the palette for different depths.   - Avinash Kaushik’s estimated speaking fee is $20,000–$30,000, his departure point is the Los Angeles airport system, and his primary speaking category is strategy and data analytics.

### Value Proposition
- **Definition:** An item that articulates the benefit, change, or useful outcome the person's work, service, or content offers to others.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's central claim concerns the benefit or outcome that readers, clients, collaborators, or a community can receive from the person's contribution.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Capabilities Profile, it emphasizes value to an audience rather than ability, and unlike Offering Description it centers the outcome rather than defining what is offered.
- **Examples:**
  - His technique-focused teaching explains the purpose of skills such as kneading, browning, roasting, and emulsifying so cooks can gain independence and durable confidence.
  - FAE describes her content as a changing mix of solo performances, creative expression, personal anecdotes, reflective moments, and playful interactions designed to showcase her character and leave followers feeling inspired, connected, and uplifted.

### Audience Profile
- **Definition:** An item that characterizes an established or intended audience through demographic, geographic, professional, behavioral, or interest-based information.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would leave unclear the composition, reach, or intended recipients of the person's work, service, site, or community.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Compatibility Criteria, it describes who the audience is or whom the work serves rather than specifying mutual-fit requirements, and unlike Site Orientation it does not primarily explain the content environment.
- **Examples:**
  - His primary audience is described as people aged 18–34, predominantly male but with substantial female participation, and globally distributed with especially large followings in English-speaking countries.
  - Intended clients include executives, business owners, physicians, attorneys, and other highly accountable professionals, as well as people making mid-career transitions, entrepreneurs confronting business-building pressures, and leaders adapting to AI and technological change.

### Compatibility Criteria
- **Definition:** An item that states the qualities, shared interests, boundaries, preferences, or working dynamics sought in compatible collaborators, clients, or participants.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary function is to define the qualities, interests, boundaries, activities, or working conditions that make a prospective collaborator, client, or participant a suitable fit.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Audience Profile, it establishes mutual-fit criteria rather than describing a recipient group, and unlike Participation Standards it concerns suitability rather than mandatory conduct after engagement.
- **Examples:**
  - Successful collaborators should be professional, respectful, and emotionally compatible, communicate openly about boundaries, preferences, and ideas, and share responsibility for developing an agreed creative vision.
  - Participation implicitly requires adherence to two table rules: “The Golden Rule; Have Fun! The Silver Rule; Don't be a Jerk!/Don't interfere with other peoples' fun!”
  - She positions her ideal client as an easygoing, attentive, warmhearted parent who prioritizes family time, meaningful experiences, lasting photography, and a simple natural aesthetic without demanding perfection, and invites such readers to recognize the fit.

### Participation Standards
- **Definition:** An item that establishes conduct requirements, participation procedures, behavioral boundaries, or enforcement measures governing interpersonal or community engagement.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate behavioral rules, procedural requirements, or enforcement boundaries governing whether or how readers may participate or engage.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Compatibility Criteria, it specifies rules participants must follow rather than preferred fit, and unlike Invitation it regulates engagement rather than encouraging it.
- **Examples:**
  - She rejects generic requests and approaches treating her home merely as free lodging; applicants should demonstrate respect by reading the profile and including at least her name or another personal sentence.
  - Alexandra firmly excludes flirting and sexual propositions, defining the platform as a place for kindness-based affection toward travel, cultures, and people rather than dating.
  - Comments may be edited or removed for spam, irrelevant links, profanity, hateful or offensive material, or personal attacks; criticism should target ideas rather than people, and the owner may moderate without notice or alter the comment policy at any time.

### Invitation
- **Definition:** An item that encourages readers to connect, collaborate, follow, respond, participate, commission work, or otherwise continue the relationship.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's main function is to ask or encourage readers to take a particular next step in relation to the person or site.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Contact Access, it motivates action rather than merely enabling communication, and unlike Recommendation it seeks relational engagement rather than advising substantive conduct.
- **Examples:**
  - A submission invitation directs short-story writers to Tall Tale TV’s guidelines.
  - A closing invitation offers a limited number of impact-based retainers to organizations seeking a transition from linear growth to peak efficiency, particularly leaders wanting a single authoritative basis for decisions.

### Contact Access
- **Definition:** A bounded component that provides usable channels or instructions for reaching the person or an authorized contact.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting the bounded item would remove the practical means by which readers can communicate with the person or responsible organization.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Invitation, it enables communication rather than persuading readers to initiate it, and unlike Service Access it supplies contact channels rather than operational service terms.
- **Examples:**
  - A practical contact block gives the phone number 07717 515 013, the location at Berkhamsted Chiropractic Clinic, 69 High Street, Berkhamsted, HP4 2DE, and Monday-to-Friday daytime and evening availability.
  - Official inquiries are directed to the corporate communications desk of BlackBuck, legally identified as Zinka Logistics Solutions Private Limited; Yabaji’s personal contact details are not publicly disclosed.

### Rapport Building
- **Definition:** A rhetorical item that creates warmth, familiarity, empathy, consolation, or interpersonal solidarity through direct relational address.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item primarily welcomes, appreciates, empathizes with, consoles, or expresses solidarity with readers without chiefly requesting action or correcting an invalidating belief.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Invitation, it builds connection without chiefly requesting a next step, and unlike Emotional Validation it does not primarily counter shame, self-blame, or doubts about worth.
- **Examples:**
  - He thanks readers, reflects on the teenage project’s growth into an internationally used parental resource, and hopes its guidance makes choosing toys easier, better informed, and more enjoyable.
  - Having lost Annie the previous February, the writer dreads another death in the same year but hopes Ranger will recover temporarily and remain with the family longer.

### Emotional Validation
- **Definition:** An item that directly affirms a reader's feelings, needs, lovability, or worth by correcting a demeaning or self-blaming interpretation of their experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a direct affirmation that counters shame, self-blame, emotional invalidation, or doubts about personal worth.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Rapport Building, it performs a specific corrective affirmation rather than chiefly creating general warmth or solidarity.
- **Examples:**
  - The blog reassures readers after unexplained rejection: “You weren't ghosted because you were too much. You were ghosted because they weren't ready for someone real.”
  - The closing affirmation tells readers, “You're not hard to love. You're just waiting for someone who knows how to stay.”

### Concept Explanation
- **Definition:** An item that defines or explains a concept, mechanism, distinction, relationship, framework, or evaluative indicator so readers can understand its meaning or operation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the definition, mechanism, distinction, framework, or indicator interpretation needed to understand a subject.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Interpretation, it develops subject-matter understanding rather than deriving broader significance from established material, and unlike Process Description it need not present a bounded sequence of activity.
- **Examples:**
  - Svadhyaya means self-study and, with tapas and ishvara pranidhana, constitutes Kriya Yoga, the action-oriented part of the ancient yogic path toward samadhi.
  - The system removes suffixes and searches with word stems across both languages, producing intentionally unusual suggested terms and topic labels described as Dumbrish.
  - A message-quality score distinguishes thoughtful questions, credible research, and constructive feedback from low-value emoji reactions and generic enthusiasm.

### Problem Framing
- **Definition:** An item that establishes or diagnoses a problem, unmet need, risk, deficiency, harmful condition, prevailing assumption, or case circumstance that warrants attention or response.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the problem, gap, harmful condition, prevailing misconception, or case-specific need that makes a response relevant.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Motivation, it establishes an external need rather than the person's internal impetus, and unlike External Context it frames a condition specifically as requiring attention or change.
- **Examples:**
  - Standard bloodwork is characterized as inadequate because it seldom assesses factors affecting DNA repair, mitochondrial function, hormones, detoxification, or immune surveillance, leaving many patients treated without being biologically understood.
  - The Social Security Administration can answer questions but cannot advise claimants, and staffing is described as being at a 50-year low; required telephone appointments and the end of office walk-ins in 2025 are said to make obtaining help difficult and time-consuming.
  - Joe and Raquel Morales explain that their search for ranch land arose from Joe’s family heritage of horsemanship, attachment to rural life, and ambition to create a family legacy; after extensive research and an unproductive search elsewhere, the Sangre de Cristo Mountain views convinced them to seek land near Westcliffe.

### Thesis Claim
- **Definition:** An item that states or restates the central arguable contention the document seeks to establish.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the document's principal contention or its deliberate restatement.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Values Statement, it advances the document's main proposition rather than the person's guiding conviction, and unlike Integrative Synthesis it need not consolidate multiple developed conclusions.
- **Examples:**
  - CoinMinutes argues from observations across hundreds of blockchain ecosystems that authentic human relationships, rather than technical complexity or marketing expenditure, are the decisive basis of lasting project success.
  - Measuring cryptocurrency communities requires analysis of human behavior and cannot be reduced to counting followers.

### Advocacy
- **Definition:** An item that advocates or opposes a substantive policy, institutional practice, public course of action, or concrete remedy for a shared issue.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate an argued stance, opposition, commitment, or proposed remedy concerning a public, professional, community, or institutional issue.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Values Statement, it advances an issue-specific course of action rather than a general conviction, and unlike Recommendation it seeks broader public or institutional change rather than chiefly guiding an individual's practical choice.
- **Examples:**
  - Young calls for educational innovation, parental choice, support for educators, and classrooms centered on learning rather than divisive politics or age-inappropriate material, with children’s individual needs as the governing objective.
  - Environmental protection should prioritize freshwater improvement and nature-based flood management, including giving rivers more space and restoring water storage around Kāpiti’s historic dune wetlands, because these measures are more sustainable and economical than continually expanding engineered infrastructure.
  - To address property taxes and discretionary spending that rose from $359,000 in 2023 to $1.2 million in 2025, the candidate proposes immediate nonessential cuts and dedicating 10% of each surplus to reserves until the city holds at least three months of expenses.

### Recommendation
- **Definition:** An item that recommends a practical choice, priority, standard, precaution, evaluative method, or course of action intended to improve decisions or outcomes.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's principal function is to advise readers or relevant actors what to choose, avoid, prioritize, consider, or do.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Invitation, it guides substantive conduct rather than relational engagement, and unlike Advocacy it does not primarily press for public, institutional, or policy change.
- **Examples:**
  - Markoski advises buyers to remain patient in a rapidly changing process, retain truthful professionals, and follow their guidance; he also recommends prioritizing sound structure and mechanical systems over inexpensive cosmetic features, warning that attractive, costly new construction may be less sound than older homes.
  - New beekeepers should not plan to remain treatment-free: they should learn Varroa biology, use resistant bees and management controls, monitor infestation, and treat when necessary because high mite levels usually kill the host colony and harm nearby colonies.
  - A practical lesson collection advises aspiring online participants to be genuine rather than performative, publish less but with greater purpose, favor connection over broadcasting, reinforce a consistent identity, and avoid burnout by pacing themselves instead of chasing trends indiscriminately.

### User Instruction
- **Definition:** An item that directs users to perform a required operational action, supply information, or interact with a tool, service, or process in a specified way.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a practical directive users must follow to complete a process or use a resource effectively.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it gives procedural directions tied to using or completing something, and unlike Process Description it tells readers what to do rather than explaining how the process is structured.
- **Examples:**
  - Guide users must gather the priority information required by the evaluation team before it can develop the post-occupancy evaluation framework, surveys, interview guides, and observation tools.
  - Queries may combine French and English keywords without full sentences; adding space-separated terms supplies more context and generally improves accuracy.

### Evidence Support
- **Definition:** An item that presents or identifies empirical, documentary, testimonial, quantitative, or observational grounds used to make a substantive proposition more credible.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate facts, research, testimony, data, artifacts, cases, observations, or source context offered chiefly to substantiate another claim.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Credibility Support, it validates a content-level claim rather than the person's standing, and unlike Finding it deploys information as support rather than chiefly reporting the result itself.
- **Examples:**
  - The U.S. Agency for Health Care Policy and Research reportedly found serious complications from specific chiropractic adjustments rare, favored adjustment before surgery, and discouraged oral steroids, antidepressants, and colchicine for acute low-back problems.
  - Searching the 78,000-page index uses 3.2 GB of RAM and takes about 0.3–0.5 seconds on a desktop; the live service typically responds within one second on shared CPU-only hosting alongside other sites and applications.
  - The eighty-year Harvard Study of Adult Development is cited as finding that relationship quality, rather than wealth, status, or achievement, was the strongest predictor of happiness.

### Explanatory Illustration
- **Definition:** An item that clarifies or exemplifies a broader claim, concept, capability, or practical implication through a concrete case, analogy, scenario, or anecdote.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item chiefly uses a concrete, hypothetical, simplified, or representative case to make a broader idea, distinction, application, or experience easier to understand.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evidence Support, it primarily aids understanding or vividness rather than establishing that a disputed claim is true, and unlike Experience Highlight it serves a broader explanatory point.
- **Examples:**
  - A Chapter Six excerpt uses house construction as an analogy for why chiropractic care must proceed in a prescribed sequence before the spine can become stable and function correctly.
  - Product stickers can communicate ingredients, barcodes, safety warnings, and instructions, making accuracy essential to avoid confusion or compliance problems.
  - A hypothetical comparison between 100,000 passive followers and 10,000 advocates active in governance and promotion frames committed participation as more valuable than audience size.

### Finding
- **Definition:** An item that reports what was found or learned through inquiry, observation, evaluation, measurement, experimentation, or analysis.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary commitment is to report a result, pattern, observation, or conclusion produced through research, evaluation, measurement, or a discrete trial.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evidence Support, it presents the result itself as the main information rather than chiefly using that result to support a separate proposition.
- **Examples:**
  - A Bridgepoint Collaboratory for Research and Innovation study published in the American Journal of Infection Control found no clear guidance for cleaning wheelchairs despite their routine presence and mechanical complexity in healthcare institutions.
  - A West Virginia cave-photography experiment used long exposures and a 20-watt halogen floodlight that worked well in large passages and caverns.

### Critical Evaluation
- **Definition:** An item that evaluates a subject by identifying its quality, effectiveness, limitations, risks, tradeoffs, performance, or suitability.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's main function is to judge the strengths, weaknesses, effectiveness, risks, limitations, performance, or suitability of a work, object, practice, experience, idea, or conduct.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Interpretation, it makes an evaluative judgment rather than chiefly explaining meaning, and unlike Evidence Support it delivers the assessment rather than merely supplying grounds for one.
- **Examples:**
  - The Ancient Hero would feel less arbitrary and punitive if players had more ways to learn about or interact with him; the language barrier hinders his alliance and explanation before taking the time stone, though page and deadline constraints are acknowledged.

### Interpretation
- **Definition:** An item that derives thematic, causal, strategic, symbolic, social, or conceptual meaning from established facts, experiences, identity choices, evidence, or work.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the principal explanation of what established facts, experiences, identity markers, evidence, or work mean or imply.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Concept Explanation, it interprets the significance of already presented material rather than teaching the subject itself, and unlike Integrative Synthesis it need not combine multiple profile strands.
- **Examples:**
  - The debut’s sequence creates an emotional progression from trauma, loss, and disorientation toward healing, acceptance, and spiritual stability, turning individually readable essays into a coherent memoir journey.
  - Anonymity is presented as enabling expression without social expectations, identity-based judgment, or personal-branding pressures, thereby supporting candid thought, creativity, and more genuine interaction.
  - The review is interpreted as evidence that comprehensive, patient-centered nurse practitioner care can improve outcomes for vulnerable populations, manage chronic illness effectively, and reduce demands on acute care services.

### Thematic Framing
- **Definition:** A rhetorical item that establishes or foregrounds a memorable interpretive theme, motif, metaphor, or formulation for understanding surrounding personal or substantive material.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a governing lens, motif, metaphor, or concentrated formulation that shapes how surrounding material is understood.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Interpretation, it supplies or emphasizes the lens itself rather than chiefly analyzing material through it, and unlike Values Statement it need not state a principle that guides the person.
- **Examples:**
  - The essay broadens the American-dream motif to immigrants seeking better lives and presents Sophia, an outwardly ordinary person rather than a celebrity or executive, as someone whose sacrifices and achievements exemplify that ideal.
  - A pull quotation condenses Steffen’s current orientation: “Discontinuity is the job.”
  - The opening motto, “Life’s too short for straight lines—so I traded my ruler for a paintbrush!”, playfully encapsulates the move from engineering to art.

### Integrative Synthesis
- **Definition:** A rhetorical item that integrates multiple preceding facts, experiences, qualities, activities, or conclusions into an overarching characterization, lesson, or final takeaway.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate an overarching interpretation or takeaway that draws together multiple previously developed aspects of the profile or discussion.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Interpretation, it consolidates several developed strands rather than interpreting one bounded subject, and unlike Legacy Assessment it need not focus on enduring significance.
- **Examples:**
  - The closing reflection presents her career as evidence that perceived limitations can be challenged and that laughter, honesty, and authentic self-acceptance can inspire hope and transformation.
  - The biography concludes that Kardashian repeatedly transformed controversy and entertainment exposure into a multibillion-dollar commercial platform and influence spanning fashion, entrepreneurship, media, and social justice, thereby reshaping the possibilities of modern celebrity on self-directed terms.
  - The profile closes by linking Issahaku’s identity, ancestral legacy, cultural commitment, Wikipedia participation, and broader educational work, presenting each contribution as part of an ongoing effort to help knowledge unite and empower people.

### Comparative Positioning
- **Definition:** An item that positions a person or approach relative to alternatives or synthesizes reasons for a favorable judgment, selection, recognition, or preference.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate an explicit argument that the person or approach is distinctive, preferable, suitable, or deserving of selection or recognition.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Credibility Support, it makes the comparative or selection judgment itself rather than merely supplying qualifications or validation, and unlike Critical Evaluation its purpose is favorable positioning.
- **Examples:**
  - Taylor claims his community presence and early work on proposed initiatives during the preceding 18 months demonstrate stronger current qualifications than Representative Bolden’s record; he respects her historic achievements and counsel but argues that those merits do not justify continued stagnation.
  - Huang is judged a strong candidate for the Best Research Article Award because of innovative self-healing and low-dielectric materials research, publication quality, and leadership; stronger evidence on citations, practical impact, and interdisciplinary collaboration would reinforce the case, particularly if the award values fundamental breakthroughs with application potential.
  - The profile distinguishes Vadali through a prevention-first approach that combines clinical rigor with everyday practicality and treats prevention as the basis of care rather than a secondary measure.

### Topical Account
- **Definition:** An item that informs readers about an external subject central to the site by presenting its facts, history, circumstances, people, or developments.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a substantive factual or historical account of an external subject that is itself central to the site's content.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike External Context, it treats the external subject as primary content rather than background used chiefly to situate the person or their work.
- **Examples:**

Alliance College rebuilt there, closed in 1987, and its buildings became a women’s correctional facility.

### Topical Update
- **Definition:** An item that briefly informs readers about a recent or forthcoming event, finding, milestone, release, image, or resource relevant to the person or site's subject matter.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a discrete time-sensitive report of a recent or imminent development relevant to the person, site, or subject area.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Current Pursuits, it foregrounds the newsworthiness and timing of a development, and unlike Topical Account it provides a discrete update rather than a fuller subject account.
- **Examples:**

### External Context
- **Definition:** An item that supplies background about an external profession, organization, institution, field, community, or social condition that situates the person's activities and significance.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate background about a profession, organization, institution, field, community, or broader condition needed to situate the person's work.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Biographical Context, it explains the surrounding environment rather than the person's own life circumstances, and unlike Topical Account the external subject serves primarily as context.
- **Examples:**

### Field Outlook
- **Definition:** An item that evaluates or forecasts the condition, potential, or likely development of a field, market, community, or environment relevant to the person's activities.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item primarily assesses or predicts the present condition, potential, or future trajectory of an external field, market, community, or environment.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Future Direction, it concerns the prospects of an external environment rather than the person's own plans, and unlike External Context it makes an outlook judgment rather than supplying background.
- **Examples:**

### Site Orientation
- **Definition:** An item that explains the site's purpose, scope, organizing concept, intended readership, or relationship to the person's broader activities.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would leave readers unclear about what the site contains, why it exists, whom it addresses, or how its content should be understood.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Identity Introduction, it characterizes the site rather than the person, and unlike Navigation it explains the content environment rather than directing movement.
- **Examples:**

### Section Framing
- **Definition:** An item that frames a local section by signaling a thematic transition, defining its scope, or explaining how the following material relates to what preceded it.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate local rhetorical framing that signals a transition and establishes the scope or relationship of the material immediately following.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Site Orientation, it organizes a local content sequence rather than the site as a whole, and unlike Navigation it frames meaning rather than providing destinations.
- **Examples:**

  - A second profile segment shifts from general self-presentation to explaining the fantasies, desires, and creative qualities she seeks in OnlyFans collaborations and personal connections.

### Navigation
- **Definition:** A bounded component that guides readers to other parts of the site or to related profile, publication, project, service, or community destinations.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the bounded item's main document-level function is to help readers locate or move among relevant destinations.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Work Showcase, it directs movement rather than presenting outputs, and unlike Supplementary Resources it organizes destinations rather than supplying additional material.
- **Examples:**

  - A contents component provides navigation among the profile’s principal topics.

### Profile Reference
- **Definition:** A bounded component that condenses key identity, biographical, professional, personal, or work-related information into an at-a-glance recap for rapid lookup.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting the bounded component would remove a consolidated, scan-friendly means of reviewing key facts or previously presented profile material.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Experience Record, it summarizes a cross-section of profile material rather than systematically recording history, and unlike Supplementary Resources it recapitulates core information rather than extending it.
- **Examples:**
  - A quick-reference profile records his full name, May 17, 1986 birth in Honolulu, family relationships, early-1990s-to-present career span, principal roles and media, performance specialties, and recognizable personal qualities.

### Experience Record
- **Definition:** A bounded reference-oriented component that systematically organizes positions, education, service, relationships, or milestones into an accessible record of experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item functions chiefly as an organized biographical record whose arrangement supports lookup, categorical review, or chronological review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Biographical Context or Life Narrative, it prioritizes systematic reference over explanation or storytelling, and unlike Profile Reference it records structured history rather than a broad recap.
- **Examples:**

### Supplementary Resources
- **Definition:** A bounded component that supplies optional materials, fuller records, reusable assets, inventories, or extended information beyond the core profile.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting the bounded component would remove optional extending material while leaving the core self-description substantially intact.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Navigation, it contributes additional material rather than guiding movement, and unlike Profile Reference it extends rather than recapitulates the core profile.
- **Examples:**

### Source Documentation
- **Definition:** A bounded component that records the sources or provenance informing document content so readers can verify its foundations or pursue the subject further.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting the bounded component would remove the document's organized record of sources used for verification, provenance assessment, or further inquiry.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evidence Support, it preserves a document-level verification trail rather than advancing one claim, and unlike Supplementary Resources its primary function is source documentation.
- **Examples:**

### Relevant Disclosure
- **Definition:** An item that transparently states affiliations, interests, constraints, commercial relationships, authorship conditions, limitations, or other interpretation-relevant circumstances.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's main purpose is transparency about a circumstance that materially affects trust, interpretation, expectations, limitations, or permitted use.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Biographical Context, it is included because the circumstance affects interpretation or trust, and unlike Reuse Governance it discloses a condition rather than regulating reuse.

### Reuse Governance
- **Definition:** An item that grants, limits, conditions, or challenges the quotation, reproduction, adaptation, linking, or other reuse of material.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate permissions, conditions, attribution requirements, or objections governing reuse of the person's or site's material.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Relevant Disclosure, it regulates treatment of material rather than merely revealing an interpretation-relevant circumstance, and unlike Acknowledgment it prescribes attribution rather than recording it.
