say, do, and include, and in what order, before those choices were realized
as particular sentences, formatting, markup, and document components.

It is an analytical representation of the document, not a claim about the
writer's actual psychological process.

The outline must capture:

- substantive content commitments;
- rhetorical progression;
- functionally meaningful structural commitments;
- the single primary function performed by each item;

while excluding extraction artifacts and abstracting away from surface
realization.


# FORMAT

Format: User Reviews

Description: First-person evaluative reviews of a product, service or place.

Use this format context to interpret document conventions and choose roles.
The document itself remains authoritative.

Do not infer content or components merely because they are conventional for
the format.


# ROLE VOCABULARY

The following is the role vocabulary for User Reviews:

### Target Identification
- **Definition:** A bounded identifying component establishes the specific subject to which the review and its evaluations apply.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would leave readers unable to determine exactly which entity, offering, location, version, or variant the review evaluates.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description or Reference Aid, it establishes the review target itself rather than characterizing it or organizing supplementary facts about it.
- **Examples:**
  - A title identifies Eurostars Danube Budapest.
  - Taylor Medical Wellness, Weight Loss and Aesthetic Group is listed at 5901 Peachtree Dunwoody Rd C25, Atlanta, Georgia 30328.

### Contextual Framing
- **Definition:** This role supplies circumstances, purposes, needs, expectations, or prior experience that frame the perspective from which the review is given.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate relevant information about the reviewer's situation, aims, needs, prior familiarity, expectations, or intended experiential perspective.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Review Framing, it explains the reviewer's perspective or situation rather than defining the document's agenda or interpretive purpose.
- **Examples:**
  - The reviewer assesses Jeslot88 Club from a serious player's perspective, prioritizing payment speed, game quality, stability, and convenience; the platform initially appears to be a balanced gaming hub for active players, with slots, live games, and region-dependent sportsbook options rather than a bonus-led promotion site.
  - The writer will test the products in her hair and later report their actual performance.

### Review Framing
- **Definition:** This role establishes the organizing purpose, planned coverage, central inquiry, or interpretive lens of a review or assembled review collection.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate an explicit framing of what review discourse or a review collection is for, will cover, centrally ask, or invite readers to consider.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Contextual Framing, it frames the document or collection rather than the reviewer's circumstances, and unlike Navigation Aid, it states the agenda rather than providing wayfinding.
- **Examples:**
  - The evaluation considers free and paid functionality and prices, audience and profile authenticity, design and usability, safety and privacy, and the likelihood of securing an encounter.
  - The collection opens by presenting personal testimonies about Jesus as prompts for readers to reflect on their own experiences, become humble, and feel profound gratitude.
  - The review proposes an impartial assessment of Legacy Healing Center’s care, facilities, staff, and overall experience to determine whether it merits distinction.

### Subject Background
- **Definition:** This role supplies the reviewed subject's origins, creator context, development history, or design intentions to explain its present form.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate historical, creator-related, developmental, or design background explaining how the reviewed subject reached its present form.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it explains origins or development rather than current characteristics, and unlike Contextual Framing, it concerns the subject rather than the reviewer.
- **Examples:**
  - Space Cat Audio Technologies began in the UK with Arron Courts and Abegael Saward modifying vintage instruments, then developed original performance-oriented devices with circuit designers John W Oram and Dave Cherry, combining practical live control with experimental circuit-bending influences.
  - The Fort Worth municipal course began as a nine-hole country club in 1924, entered city ownership in 1938, was redesigned in the early 1960s, and reopened after its 2024 centennial following a multimillion-dollar renovation lasting more than two years.
  - The company is said to have been founded by parents who wanted mobility after having children to be less restrictive, leading them to create baby gear that folds rapidly, packs compactly, and works reliably in varied settings.

### Factual Description
- **Definition:** This role reports non-evaluative characteristics, features, conditions, arrangements, operations, or recurring processes associated with the reviewed subject.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item is primarily present to state what the subject, setting, feature, condition, operation, or recurring process is like without organizing that information as evaluation, interpretation, or a specific episode.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Aspect Evaluation, it does not chiefly assign quality or value, and unlike Experience Account, it is not organized around a particular event or interaction.
- **Examples:**
  - The brand’s website offers one unit for €59.99 at a claimed 50% discount, or three for €164.99 with two additional units as gifts, described as a 72% discount.
  - Selected Arabica seed spends one year in a nursery before transplantation into straight field rows spaced three meters apart with 1.5-meter row widths; the initial harvest occurs after 18 months and is termed a fly crop.

### Content Synopsis
- **Definition:** This role summarizes the narrative, arguments, subject matter, scope, or internal progression of a content-bearing reviewed work.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a non-evaluative summary of the narrative, arguments, subject matter, scope, or internal progression represented within a reviewed work.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it condenses what a work presents internally, and unlike Experience Account, it does not recount an episode undergone by the reviewer.
- **Examples:**
  - The book’s largest part, comprising 11 chapters across about 80 pages, examines supposed truths, partial truths, and myths involving Heinrich’s triangle, zero-accident aspirations, human error, priorities, numerical indicators, and attempts to measure safety.
  - San Francisco police lieutenant Ed Cullen is secretly involved with wealthy married Lois Frazer; after Lois fatally shoots her estranged husband Howard when he returns to rob her home, Ed protects her by moving the body to an airport parking lot.
  - A paired expectation-setting summary promises practical knowledge about choosing or building smokers, managing fire and smoke, buying quality meat, 11 restaurant recipes, espresso, and beer, while clarifying that readers will not receive hundreds of secret recipes or easy shortcuts.

### Experience Account
- **Definition:** This role recounts a substantively unified event, interaction, use episode, transaction, or sequence from the reviewer's experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a coherent account of what the reviewer encountered, did, received, or experienced over time.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it is organized around a particular episode, and unlike Outcome Report, it emphasizes what happened rather than chiefly the resulting change or endpoint.
- **Examples:**
  - M reports in April 2023 that James made her first sexual experience painless and taught her how to please him, leaving her feeling transformed into a woman.
  - Removing gluten, dairy, sugar, and other foods initially improved her condition enough that she tapered off medication, believing nutritional health might provide the answer.

### Outcome Report
- **Definition:** This role reports a result, change, or consequential state produced through engagement with the reviewed subject or service.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a reported result, change, or consequential state produced through engagement with the reviewed subject, without primarily removing a developed episode or evaluative argument.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Experience Account, it centers on the resulting change or endpoint, and unlike Evaluation Rationale, it reports that outcome as the primary information rather than chiefly as support for a judgment.
- **Examples:**
  - After nine months, Sonya had fallen from 247 to 188 pounds; although her goal is 150 pounds, she expects to reach and maintain it with support from Dr. Majid’s team.
  - A brief postoperative progress report records a decline from 271 pounds on October 1 to 256 after two weeks on a liquid diet and 187 four months after surgery.

### Interpretation
- **Definition:** This role derives or explains a meaning, theme, causal principle, symbolic pattern, conceptual relationship, or broader significance conveyed by the reviewed subject or experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the reviewer's derivation of meaning, thematic significance, explanatory principle, conceptual relationship, or broader implication from the subject or associated evidence.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it infers significance beyond direct characteristics, and unlike Evaluation Rationale, its main purpose is explanation or interpretation rather than warranting a quality judgment.
- **Examples:**
  - After considering secret recipes, unusual skills, privileged meat sources, and special wood as possible explanations for Franklin’s success, the reviewer concludes that passion and exceptionally hard work are decisive.
  - New York and Singapore externalize different dimensions of Lucie’s identity: New York enables freedom and reinvention, while Singapore embodies family, history, belonging, communal judgment, and tradition.
  - The campground's legacy is said to demonstrate local demand for well-managed, conveniently located places where Michigan residents can enjoy nature and spend time with loved ones.

### Evaluation Criteria
- **Definition:** This role establishes the criteria, principles, conditions, or indicators by which the reviewed subject or one of its aspects should be judged.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate standards, principles, conditions, or indicators established for judging the subject, before any primary judgment applying them is made.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Comparative Assessment, it establishes a benchmark without chiefly applying it, and unlike Review Framing, it defines standards of judgment rather than merely naming areas the review will cover.
- **Examples:**
  - Trust should be assessed through visible licensing information, responsible-gaming tools, and account protections; missing or obscure disclosures warrant greater caution.
  - Responsible guidance should foster honest communication, mutual respect, and authenticity rather than manipulation or self-alteration undertaken solely to satisfy a partner.

### Testing Method
- **Definition:** This role describes the setup, procedure, inputs, measurements, or controlled conditions used to test and assess the reviewed subject.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate the setup, procedure, inputs, measurements, or controlled variations used to generate and interpret evaluative observations.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evaluation Rationale, it explains how observations were produced rather than presenting those observations as grounds for a judgment, and unlike Basis Documentation, it is substantive method description rather than a bounded provenance record.
- **Examples:**
  - A Korg MS-20 Mini test deliberately varies loud oscillator combinations, relative phase, detuning, filter sweeps, and resonance to expose how the unit responds to changing harmonic complexity and reduced synthesizer headroom.
  - Because 12V kettles are slower than mains models and may drain leisure batteries, Practical Caravan tests the time and battery capacity required to boil 300ml, equivalent to a large mug.

### Aspect Evaluation
- **Definition:** This role judges the quality, value, adequacy, appeal, or performance of a specific aspect of the reviewed subject or experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's central commitment is a positive, negative, or mixed judgment about a particular feature, quality, interaction, or dimension of the reviewed subject.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Overall Verdict, it evaluates a bounded aspect rather than the subject as a whole, and unlike Comparative Assessment, its judgment does not depend on an explicit benchmark or alternative.
- **Examples:**
  - Discovering how areas connect and revisiting them for hidden rewards makes exploration exceptionally absorbing and difficult to stop playing.
  - Users also commend the smooth central focusing wheel for fast, precise adjustment and the multi-coated lenses for better light transmission and brightness. A forum reviewer says, “The focus wheel is very smooth and easy to adjust, and the image quality is consistently excellent thanks to the high-quality coatings.”

### Comparative Assessment
- **Definition:** This role evaluates the reviewed subject by explicitly contrasting it with a benchmark, alternative, expectation, representation, or prior condition.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary judgment depends on explicitly relating the subject to an alternative, expectation, claim, standard, representation, or prior condition.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Aspect Evaluation, the relative relationship is essential to its judgment, and unlike Evaluation Criteria, it applies rather than merely establishes the benchmark.
- **Examples:**
  - The generic, dated home page resembles competing hookup sites, although profiles shown there were also visibly active in the service's feed.
  - Users reportedly create slides 60% faster than with PowerPoint because automated design decisions reduce formatting work and leave more attention for accuracy and narrative structure.

### Evaluation Rationale
- **Definition:** This role supplies reasons, observations, examples, consequences, or causal explanations intended chiefly to support an evaluative claim.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's principal reason for inclusion is to make an evaluative claim credible or intelligible by supplying its observations, examples, causes, consequences, or other grounds.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, Experience Account, or Outcome Report, it is selected when supporting an evaluation is the item's dominant purpose rather than independently describing, recounting, or reporting.
- **Examples:**
  - Torn curtains, a damaged headboard, and pervasive wear showed that visible maintenance problems had not been corrected before occupancy.
  - AskGamblers and CasinoFreak commonly report delayed payouts and unresponsive support, while Wizard of Odds warns about excessively slow payments and poor service; the reviewer stops short of calling the casino fraudulent but advises guarded participation.

### Overall Verdict
- **Definition:** This role states or synthesizes the reviewer's overall judgment of the reviewed subject or total experience.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item chiefly communicates the reviewer's integrated bottom-line assessment of the entire reviewed subject or total experience.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Aspect Evaluation, it integrates the subject at the whole-review level, and unlike Recommendation, it concludes what the reviewer thinks rather than directing what readers should do.
- **Examples:**
  - The overall assessment presents LimaMAR as a compelling provider of dependable, economical, and efficient global freight forwarding because of its comprehensive services, customer focus, and effective technology use.
  - Leo Man Secrets may be useful but is not a guaranteed solution; its value depends on realistic expectations, selective application, personal judgment, and integration with lived relationship experience.

### Recommendation
- **Definition:** This role advises prospective users whether, when, or for whom the reviewed subject is an appropriate choice.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item primarily tells prospective users whether to choose, avoid, continue with, or consider the subject, including the audiences or conditions for which that advice applies.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Overall Verdict, it directs a future choice, and unlike Practical Guidance, it addresses whether or for whom to choose rather than how to proceed.
- **Examples:**
  - The hotel is unsuitable for guests prioritizing sleep, people sensitive to musty odors, special-occasion travelers, those expecting normal Marriott upkeep, visitors using their room extensively, and anyone troubled by conspicuous damage.
  - The review recommends Nanonets as a serious option for organizations seeking less manual entry and more automated workflows, balancing its usability, accuracy, integrations, and support against potentially high pricing and input-dependent performance; it is presented as suitable for both small teams and larger operations.

### Practical Guidance
- **Definition:** This role gives actionable tips, precautions, workarounds, logistical particulars, or usage advice for engaging with the reviewed subject.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate actionable know-how for obtaining, visiting, operating, navigating, or improving an interaction with the reviewed subject.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it explains how to proceed rather than whether to choose, and unlike Risk Warning, its primary commitment is actionable know-how rather than identification of a possible harm.
- **Examples:**
  - The 580-yard sixth reverses the former fourth and is the course’s longest hole. A right bunker creates a distance-versus-position dilemma, wind and a brook complicate the likely three-shot route, and an obscured landing area left of the green provides room for an aggressive attempt in two.
  - A practical information block gives the location as 10300 W Charleston Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89135, with hours of 11 AM–9:30 PM Monday through Friday and 11 AM–10 PM Saturday and Sunday.

### Risk Warning
- **Definition:** This role warns prospective users about harms, losses, vulnerabilities, adverse outcomes, or failures of recourse that may result from engaging with the reviewed subject.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary function is to alert prospective users to a concrete harm, loss, vulnerability, adverse outcome, or failure of recourse associated with engagement.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Practical Guidance, it primarily identifies what may go wrong rather than explaining how to proceed, and unlike Evaluation Rationale, the warning to users is itself the principal function.
- **Examples:**
  - Customers risk being charged without ever receiving a package.
  - Customers may have their card information compromised, leading to unauthorized purchases, overcharging, or repeated deductions.

### Alternatives
- **Definition:** This role identifies alternative products, services, resources, or courses of action that could address the need associated with the reviewed subject.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary contribution is to identify other products, services, resources, or courses of action capable of addressing the relevant need without chiefly ranking or endorsing them.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it expands the available choice set without chiefly advising which option to select, and unlike Comparative Assessment, it need not judge alternatives against one another.
- **Examples:**
  - Alternatives include personalized relationship counseling, professional compatibility readings, books on communication and intimacy, and direct conversations with the partner about his needs and desires.

### Improvement Proposal
- **Definition:** This role proposes a change to the reviewed subject intended to remedy a shortcoming or improve its design, performance, value, usability, or operation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a substantive proposal to change the reviewed subject in order to remedy a deficiency or improve future performance or usefulness.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Aspect Evaluation, it advocates what should be changed rather than merely judging the current state, and unlike Remedial Action, it is a reviewer's proposal rather than a responsible party's corrective commitment.
- **Examples:**
  - The reviewer recommends automated selections of suitable profiles delivered by email to reduce the time users must spend configuring and browsing the feed.
  - A replaceable battery and better main camera would improve the device, although removable-battery packaging would probably enlarge the phone or reduce capacity; camera quality may be easier to improve in a future model or possibly through software.

### Future Outlook
- **Definition:** This role projects likely future developments, trajectories, performance, adoption, or transformations relevant to the reviewed subject or its broader domain.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary contribution is a forecast or extrapolation about how the reviewed subject or its relevant domain may develop, perform, or gain significance.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Overall Verdict, it predicts what may happen rather than synthesizing present quality, and unlike Contextual Framing, it projects beyond current circumstances.
- **Examples:**
  - Exponential technological improvement will move beyond the present balance of size, cost, capability, and utility as gesture recognition, wearable computing, energy harvesting, and three-dimensional eyewear increasingly integrate personal computers with their users.
  - The review closes by projecting that continued improvement could make Meoo an industry-standard tool for AI-assisted cloud development.

### Claim Qualification
- **Definition:** This role limits or calibrates a claim or evaluation by identifying uncertainty, subjectivity, scope conditions, or constraints on its applicability.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate a limitation on the certainty, scope, applicability, universality, or generalizability of another claim or evaluation.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it primarily constrains how another claim should be interpreted, and unlike Contextual Framing, it qualifies the force of a claim rather than establishing the reviewer's perspective.
- **Examples:**
  - A closing qualification states that system range varies with factors including battery power, rider weight, terrain, riding style and speed, tyre pressure, and the selected assistance level.
  - Because numerical ratings depend on personal taste and evaluators' criteria, no universal score is asserted, though the product has acquired substantial recognition and a significant following.

### Encouragement
- **Definition:** This role reassures or emboldens readers by countering hopelessness, defeat, or fear and affirming that improvement or meaningful action remains possible.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary effect is to restore hope, confidence, or resolve in readers facing fear, discouragement, or apparent defeat.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it primarily changes the reader's outlook or resolve rather than advising whether to choose the reviewed subject, and unlike Practical Guidance, it need not prescribe a procedure.
- **Examples:**
  - Shoshi discloses that her former hopelessness included suicidal thoughts and urges people suffering from PTSD or diagnostic labels not to assume they are beyond recovery.
  - The testimonial closes by emphasizing how psychological distress can immobilize people and prevent desired lives, while assuring readers that help and hope remain available, urging them to reach out, and affirming that the effort is worthwhile.

### Reviewer Appreciation
- **Definition:** This role directly expresses the reviewer's gratitude, affection, or appreciative recognition toward the reviewed subject or people associated with it.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would chiefly eliminate a reviewer's direct expression of gratitude, affection, or appreciative regard toward the reviewed party or its representatives.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Feedback Acknowledgment, it conveys appreciation from the reviewer toward the reviewed party rather than responsively recognizing a review or concern.
- **Examples:**
  - Henry’s family thanks the staff for doing everything possible during his illness and says its compassion when he had to be put to rest will remain unforgettable.
  - R offers affectionate thanks to James in August 2018.
  - The parents of Anany Kumar Rai, an L.K.G. Blue student, open by expressing gratitude to the school and his class teacher, Mrs. Priyanka Sinha.

### Feedback Acknowledgment
- **Definition:** This role acknowledges a prior review or concern and manages the interpersonal relationship by expressing recognition, gratitude, regret, empathy, or validation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's main communicative job is to recognize a review or reviewer through thanks, apology, empathy, validation, regret, or similar responsive acknowledgment.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Reviewer Appreciation, it responds to feedback from the reviewed party's side, and unlike Remedial Action, it does not chiefly report or promise a corrective measure.
- **Examples:**
  - The page frames the testimonials as a recent selection of client feedback that the firm values, appreciates, and willingly publishes.
  - The developer expresses appreciation and invites the customer to request further assistance.

### Engagement Request
- **Definition:** This role asks a participant to provide information, initiate contact, revisit an issue, or take another step that enables continued engagement or resolution.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's chief purpose is to solicit information, contact, a response, a return visit, or another step that enables continued engagement or resolution.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Practical Guidance or Recommendation, it solicits action from a participant in the exchange rather than advising prospective users, and unlike Ancillary Promotion, it does not chiefly seek uptake of a separate offering.
- **Examples:**
  - Prospective clients are invited to schedule a complimentary, pressure-free Zoom or Skype conversation about their health and life goals and whether working together would be a suitable fit.
  - Readers are invited to report changed or additional stall information in the comments so the publication can verify and update its listing as part of a shared Singapore food-news community.

### Provider Promotion
- **Definition:** This role promotes the reviewed provider or subject through favorable self-presentation, claimed qualifications, commitments, capabilities, or affiliated endorsement.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when removing the item would eliminate provider- or affiliate-authored favorable positioning intended chiefly to build audience interest or confidence in the reviewed offering.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Aspect Evaluation or Recommendation, it advances favorable promotional positioning from the provider or an affiliate rather than an independent reviewer's judgment.
- **Examples:**
  - The operator invites travelers to explore the Patagonian fjords and Fuegian channels, grounding its approach in more than 20 years of tourism operations, nearly 30 years of collaborative research, and a goal of fostering respectful, meaningful connections with the region.
  - The company claims five years of operating in Colorado’s Rocky Mountains, where professionally trained chauffeurs uphold high standards and provide punctual, guest-focused service in all weather, promising dependable and memorable transportation during visits to Aspen Snowmass.
  - Laura Main said: “I’ve been waiting a long time for an adventure like this to come along and now that it has I am ready to swap the surgery for the swamp in one of my favourite musicals. Shrek has made a believer out of me and I can’t wait for this fairytale to take me across the country.”

### Ancillary Promotion
- **Definition:** This role presents or promotes an ancillary commercial, reciprocal, donation, membership, referral, or participation opportunity to encourage audience uptake.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary job is to present or encourage uptake of a separate offer, service, program, membership, referral, or participation opportunity associated with the review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it seeks uptake of an ancillary opportunity rather than advising about the reviewed target, and unlike Engagement Request, its primary purpose is participation or conversion rather than continued dialogue or resolution.
- **Examples:**
  - Through the free reader program, the author offers any reader a complimentary copy for an honest review; the parties arrange the copy format and review sites through private email.
  - A health-assessment offer associated with Dr. Ryan Goodkin promises a rapid evaluation, personalized wellness report, and recommendations while disclaiming medical-advice status.
  - A promotional callout encourages readers to buy Walt Disney World tickets through Expedia to earn One Key Cash rewards, receive member hotel pricing, and obtain other travel benefits.

### Purchase Facilitation
- **Definition:** A bounded commercial component facilitates acquisition of the reviewed subject by presenting a direct purchase opportunity, transactional access, current price, or availability.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded commercial component would remove the document's direct opportunity, channel, or current terms for acquiring the reviewed subject.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Recommendation, it enables or presents a transaction rather than advising whether to buy, and unlike Reference Aid, it facilitates acquisition rather than merely organizing terms for lookup.
- **Examples:**
  - A purchase prompt offers the Bagsmart six-piece Compression Packing Cube Set for $39.99, reduced from its usual $42.99 price.

### Support Solicitation
- **Definition:** This role solicits financial, material, promotional, or other support intended to sustain or expand the publisher, platform, organization, or community presenting the review.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item primarily asks readers to provide financial, material, promotional, or comparable support for the publisher, platform, organization, or community presenting the review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Engagement Request, it seeks support for the presenting organization or its mission rather than a response continuing the review exchange, and unlike Ancillary Promotion, the requested benefit flows principally to the publisher or community.
- **Examples:**
  - A fundraising appeal explains that SabersEdge depends on readers and requests support through Patreon, social-media sharing, affiliate book purchases, wish-list donations, or gifts mailed to PO Box 433, Leavenworth, KS 66048; these actions are framed as helping expand the site and mobilize Western patriots.

### Sign-Off
- **Definition:** This role provides rhetorical closure through a farewell, catchphrase, joke, aphorism, or comparable concluding flourish.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary contribution is to end the review with a stylistic farewell, catchphrase, joke, aphorism, or comparable closing flourish.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Overall Verdict, it closes the discourse stylistically rather than synthesizing the reviewer's substantive assessment.
- **Examples:**
  - The review ends with the ironic moderation maxim, “Everything in moderation, folks, including moderation.”

### Evaluation Synopsis
- **Definition:** A bounded summary component compresses the reviewer's judgment into standardized ratings, category assessments, or concise strengths and weaknesses for rapid interpretation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when a bounded component is included chiefly to give an at-a-glance synthesis of the review's evaluative stance rather than to develop the judgment in ordinary discourse.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Overall Verdict, it performs a document-level synopsis function, and unlike Reference Aid, it chiefly condenses evaluative stance rather than organizing mixed factual or practical information.
- **Examples:**
  - A concise advantages-and-disadvantages summary praises the balanced asymmetrical design, three-day movement, gold-and-champagne styling, everyday comfort, durability, and timelessness, while noting scarce availability and the possibility that manual winding will deter buyers who prefer automatic watches.
  - A condensed assessment adds Bitcoin exposure, an accessible interface, and a relatively low cash-out minimum as benefits, while warning that survey value is inconsistent, offer walls can feel repetitive or spam-like, and earnings are unsuitable as reliable full-time income.

### Transparency Disclosure
- **Definition:** This role reveals incentives, relationships, conflicts, responsibilities, or other relevant conditions needed to interpret the review's independence or trustworthiness.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's main purpose is transparency about a relationship, incentive, conflict, responsibility, or condition that could materially affect how readers assess the review's independence or trustworthiness.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Basis Documentation, it exposes potentially consequential interests or responsibilities rather than recording the review's experiential provenance, and unlike Content Status, it does not chiefly explain publication state.
- **Examples:**
  - Broker compensation and compensation-sharing arrangements are not established or directed by law, REALTOR associations, multiple listing services, or other listing services; each broker independently sets negotiable fees.
  - An affiliate disclosure states that Consumer Ability participates in the Amazon Associates Program and receives compensation from qualifying purchases.

### Attribution
- **Definition:** A bounded attribution component records who supplied a review or response or created, originated, or supplied reviewed or referenced material so responsibility and provenance are clear.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when a bounded credit is chiefly present to establish who supplied the review or response or who created, originated, or supplied reviewed or referenced material.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Target Identification, it records responsibility for a contribution or material rather than what is being reviewed, and unlike Basis Documentation, it documents authorship rather than the underlying experience or test basis.
- **Examples:**
  - A closing source note attributes the review to Bard, Google AI, and records both publication and access on January 24, 2024.
  - A closing credit attributes the source short film to Thijs Meuwese and Kris Patmo.

### Basis Documentation
- **Definition:** A bounded reference component documents the timing, type, duration, verification, equipment, or other provenance of the experience or transaction underlying the review.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded record would remove documented facts about the timing, type, duration, verification, equipment, or other provenance of the experience or transaction underlying the review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Contextual Framing, it records the review's basis for reference rather than developing the reviewer's perspective, and unlike Testing Method, it documents provenance rather than explaining an assessment procedure.
- **Examples:**
  - The Premium products arrived in a large box with an information card; the reviewed shipment was version 22, weighed 2.80 pounds, and included access to March BoxyLuxe spoilers.
  - An associated-equipment component documents the reviewer’s reference speakers, headphones, amplification, converters, computer sources, cables, interconnects, digital link, and power conditioner.

### Supplementary Material
- **Definition:** A bounded supplementary component provides supporting, illustrative, or elaborative material beyond the main review discourse.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the extracted item represents a bounded addition whose main document-level purpose is to extend, illustrate, or substantiate the review with inspectable ancillary material.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evaluation Rationale, it labels the ancillary component's document-level function rather than a substantive supporting observation, and unlike Source Documentation, it does not chiefly record external works consulted.
- **Examples:**
  - An embedded video review supplements the written assessment before the article turns to comparison with an alternative service.
  - An appended user-review collection supplies firsthand positive and negative accounts of the campground's facilities, location, value, and management practices.

### Content Status
- **Definition:** A bounded status component communicates the review's accessibility, translation, revision, publication, or moderation condition so readers can interpret the content instance they can see.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when a bounded notice is included chiefly to explain why review content is available, unavailable, altered, translated, filtered, removed, revised, or otherwise presented in its current state.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Transparency Disclosure, it explains the content's operational or publication state rather than interests or responsibilities, and unlike Basis Documentation, it does not document the reviewed experience.
- **Examples:**
  - The document is an English translation of the reviewer’s original assessment published in NVVK Info 2018/02 in May 2018.
  - A currency note records that the review was last updated on July 23, 2025.

### Review Collection
- **Definition:** A bounded collection component assembles and organizes multiple participants' substantive reviews, testimonials, experiences, or feedback as a browsable body of user commentary.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove an organized collection of multiple participants' substantive reviews, testimonials, experiences, suggestions, or other feedback.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Evaluation Synopsis, it preserves distinct participant accounts rather than compressing their judgments, and unlike Reception Record, it presents reviews of the subject rather than reactions to the review document.
- **Examples:**
  - A reverse-chronological collection presents dated testimonials from individual and coupled clients about their experiences with James.
  - A review component reports an Excellent rating from 50 Google reviews and presents dated testimonials praising George and his team for knowledgeable drivers, rapid last-minute accommodations, flight monitoring, schedule flexibility, clean spacious vehicles, child seats, punctuality, safety, comfort, and reliable airport, hotel, and activity transfers despite limited alternatives and difficult mountain conditions.
  - A reverse-chronological guestbook (2006–2024) presents attributed reader comments praising usability, spiritual encouragement, and sovereign-grace teaching; recording practical interests and suggestions; disputing George Ella’s account of NCT; and quoting “Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, He explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures concerning Himself,” (Luke 24:27).

### Navigation Aid
- **Definition:** A bounded navigation component provides locators or pathways that help readers find and move among portions of the review or continue to related, canonical, comparative, or otherwise relevant content.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove document-level wayfinding to portions of the review, associated content, canonical instances, related reviews, or external resources.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Review Framing, it enables access or movement rather than merely previewing coverage, and unlike Supplementary Material, it routes readers to content rather than itself supplying the ancillary material.
- **Examples:**
  - A timestamped viewing guide directs readers to the video’s three successive points: altered neurophysiology from 0:00, changed cerebellar connectivity from 0:12, and associated improvements in objective well-being measures from 0:26.
  - Readers are directed to the clean main review page as the canonical source, while referral-page versions may be shared for affiliate attribution if they point back to that main page.
  - A navigational callout directs readers seeking additional help to a separate, extensive strategy guide for Forbidden Desert.

### Reference Aid
- **Definition:** A bounded reference component organizes key factual, logistical, technical, acquisition, comparative, or question-oriented information for efficient consultation outside the main review discourse.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove a dedicated quick-lookup resource that consolidates subject facts, logistics, specifications, acquisition terms, comparisons, common answers, or unresolved audience questions.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description or Practical Guidance, it performs a document-level lookup function, and unlike Evaluation Synopsis, it does not chiefly compress the reviewer's evaluative stance.
- **Examples:**
  - A practical information block credits Dan Souter with the 1925 design and Alister MacKenzie with a 1926 bunkering plan; notes private status and $300 AUD access for reciprocal and international visitors; and provides membership and official-site resources, +61 3 8558 2700, and the Cheltenham, Victoria address.
  - A bounded comparison display provides a quick feature-by-feature view of the available mobile editions.
  - A frequently asked questions component reiterates the protein sources, competitive serving-level nutrition, and suitability for active lifestyles; acknowledges taste and texture concerns; states that the product is dairy- and soy-free while advising sensitivity checks; and directs buyers to selected online retailers and the official site for premium-priced purchasing.

### Reference Definition
- **Definition:** A bounded reference component establishes the meaning, criteria, or constituent elements of a key term, concept, classification, or model for consistent interpretation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove the controlling meaning, criteria, or constituent elements assigned to a key term, concept, classification, or model.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, it establishes a controlling conceptual meaning rather than characterizing the reviewed subject, and unlike Reference Aid, definition rather than general lookup is its primary function.
- **Examples:**
  - A bounded four-part definition of manhood is introduced, but the four propositions themselves are not recoverable from the supplied document.

### Source Documentation
- **Definition:** A bounded source component records external works, resources, or authorities consulted, cited, or offered for further reading so readers can trace or extend the review's informational basis.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove the document's organized, traceable record of external works, resources, or authorities supporting, informing, or extending the review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Basis Documentation, it records external informational sources rather than the experience underlying the review, and unlike Supplementary Material, documentation of source provenance is its primary purpose.
- **Examples:**
  - A five-entry bibliography documents general self-help works concerning finding love, love languages, sustaining marriage, gendered relationship communication, and recovery from harmful parenting.
  - A source section lists preparedness resources from the American Red Cross, FEMA, and DHS alongside Alton Brown’s 2009 book Gear Up: Ultimate Kitchen Kit.

### Corrective Clarification
- **Definition:** This role reactively supplies information that corrects, disputes, disambiguates, or materially contextualizes an earlier account or evaluation.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item is chiefly intended to correct, contest, disambiguate, or materially contextualize a claim made or implied in a prior review.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Factual Description, its defining function is corrective engagement with a prior claim, and unlike Feedback Acknowledgment, it changes or challenges the informational account rather than merely recognizing it.

### Remedial Action
- **Definition:** This role reports, offers, or promises action intended to correct a problem, remedy harm, resolve a complaint, or prevent recurrence.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when the item's primary contribution is to document a corrective measure, resolution step, compensation, change, or commitment prompted by a reported problem.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Improvement Proposal, it records action by a responsible participant rather than a reviewer's suggested change, and unlike Engagement Request, it states what has been or will be done rather than asking another participant to act.

### Reception Record
- **Definition:** A bounded reception component records audience responses to the review, such as helpfulness assessments, reactions, endorsements, or aggregate engagement signals.
- **Assignment test:** Select this role when omitting a bounded component would remove the document's record of how other users received, rated, endorsed, or otherwise appraised the review itself.
- **Distinguished from:** Unlike Review Collection, it documents reception of the review document rather than reviews of the subject, and unlike Feedback Acknowledgment, it records reception rather than expressing a substantive responsive message.

Use only:

- the exact role names supplied above;
- or the reserved role `Other`.

Do not:

- invent a role;
- rename a role;
- combine role names;
- subdivide a role;
- assign multiple roles to one item.


# TARGET REPRESENTATION

A competent writer given only the outline should be able to produce a
substantively, rhetorically, and structurally equivalent document.

The reconstruction must preserve:

- claims, facts, events, examples, evidence, decisions, contrasts,
  objections, responses, consequences, conclusions, and other substantive
  commitments;
- the order in which those commitments are introduced;
- significant analogies, metaphors, and descriptions when they carry
  substantive meaning;
- load-bearing names, quantities, dates, identifiers, quotations, and
  exact wording;
- distinctions between the writer's claims and attributed material;
- bounded components that perform meaningful organizational, navigational,
  attributional, documentary, interpretive, supplementary, legal, or other
  communicative functions.

The reconstruction need not preserve:

- original wording or syntax except when exact wording is substantive;
- sentence, clause, line, paragraph, section, or stanza boundaries;
- transitional phrasing;
- repetition used only for rhythm or emphasis;
- incidental examples or descriptive details;
- stylistic ornament without substantive function;
- purely visual formatting;
- exact heading, numbering, citation, reference, or markup style;
- commands or notation controlling only rendering or layout;
- administrative metadata without a substantive, rhetorical, or structural
  function;
- artifacts introduced by scraping, conversion, OCR, markup exposure,
  interface capture, or file extraction.


# WHAT COUNTS AS AN ITEM

An item represents one locally continuous commitment in the latent plan.

A commitment may be:

1. SUBSTANTIVE: a claim, fact, event, example, method, finding, decision,
   recommendation, or other content contribution;

2. RHETORICAL: a move that frames, motivates, qualifies, supports,
   contrasts, interprets, or concludes other content;

3. STRUCTURAL: a bounded component included to organize, navigate,
   attribute, document, supplement, disclose, or otherwise support the
   document's communicative function.

Possible structural commitments include:

- an abstract or executive summary;
- a contents or navigation component;
- a glossary or collection of defined terms;
- a source or reference section;
- an appendix or supplementary section;
- an acknowledgments, disclosure, attribution, or contribution section;
- a bounded collection of notes;
- a table, figure, code block, equation group, or data display contributing
  information as a unified component.

An item is not necessarily one sentence, clause, fact, action, image,
paragraph, section, or stanza. It may contain several details when they
jointly perform the same governing move or structural function.

Give a supporting example, evidentiary case, event, explanation, or
consequence its own item when it makes an independently meaningful
contribution.

Keep details that merely complete, qualify, restate, justify, facilitate,
or implement one governing move within that move's item.


# GOVERNING-QUESTION PRINCIPLE

An item should normally answer one practical, narrative, descriptive,
argumentative, documentary, or structural question, such as:

- What happened?
- What claim is being advanced?
- What evidence supports or challenges it?
- What rule applies?
- What should the reader do?
- What caused this result?
- What does this example demonstrate?
- How is something characterized?
- What conclusion follows?
- What bounded component is included, and what function does it perform?
- What material is documented, attributed, summarized, supplemented, or
  made available for reference?

Keep conditions, exceptions, rationales, incidental examples, resources,
indicators, and implementation together when they answer the same immediate
question.

Split when the document begins answering a different question or makes a
separately planned contribution, even if both concern the same broad topic.


# CANONICAL GRANULARITY

When multiple segmentations are plausible:

- represent one governing point with its conditions, exceptions, rationale,
  consequences, resources, indicators, and implementation as one item;
- represent one bounded component with its internal entries as one item
  when those entries jointly perform one documentary function;
- split a distinct claim, action, case, event, decision, objection,
  response, conclusion, or structural component when it performs an
  independently meaningful function.

Do not create one item per entry in a collection unless an entry is itself
discussed, evaluated, quoted, contrasted, or otherwise foregrounded.

When uncertain, choose the least fragmented segmentation that preserves
every independently meaningful substantive, rhetorical, and structural
commitment.


# ROLE-AWARE SEGMENTATION

The role vocabulary may help identify boundaries, but roles do not
determine boundaries by themselves.

First identify candidate commitments using meaning, contiguity, governing
questions, and independence. Then use the vocabulary to test those
candidates.

A likely change in primary role supports a boundary only when the document
also introduces an independently meaningful commitment.

Do not split merely because:

- one unified move has several secondary effects;
- several roles could plausibly describe the move;
- a condition, exception, rationale, or illustration has a different
  secondary function;
- splitting would make role assignment easier;
- splitting would avoid assigning `Other`.

Do not merge merely because:

- adjacent moves would receive the same role;
- they concern the same topic;
- they contribute to the same broad purpose;
- merging would avoid assigning `Other`.

If a candidate appears to perform multiple functions, ask:

"Does this region contain multiple independently planned commitments, or
one commitment with a primary function and secondary effects?"

Split only in the first case. Otherwise, keep it unified and assign the role
representing its primary function.


# PARAPHRASE AND STRUCTURAL INVARIANCE

Two versions differing only in wording, syntax, sentence boundaries,
paragraphing, formatting, markup, numbering, or citation style should
produce equivalent outlines with approximately the same:

- items;
- order;
- boundaries;
- granularity;
- global themes;
- role assignments.

Therefore:

- do not use grammatical or formatting boundaries alone to define items;
- do not split because material appears in separate sentences or blocks;
- do not merge because distinct moves appear in one sentence or section;
- do not let headings determine item count;
- do not treat rendering syntax, numbering, or citation style as content;
- do not assign roles from surface wording or formatting;
- do treat addition or removal of a functionally meaningful component as a
  possible structural change.

For every boundary and role assignment, ask whether it would remain the
same if the commitment were expressed with entirely different wording and
formatting.


## OUTPUT LANGUAGE

Invariance extends across natural languages. Two documents differing only in
the language they are written in should produce equivalent outlines.

Write every field of the output in English, whatever language the source
document is written in:

- `document_description`, `global_themes`, and every item's `content` are
  English prose;
- translate quoted material rather than reproducing it in the source script;
- give personal, place, and organisation names in their standard English form
  where one exists, and otherwise transliterate;
- leave numerals, dates, and quantities as the document states them.

Do not place source-script text anywhere in the output. Do not add a
translation note and do not remark on the source language: the outline records
what the document commits to, not the language it used to do so.

# STEP 0 — FILTER EXTRACTION AND INGESTION ARTIFACTS

Treat the input as a potentially noisy representation of the intended
document.

Ignore material clearly introduced by scraping, conversion, OCR, markup
exposure, interface capture, or file extraction, including:

- raw rendering tags and isolated markup tokens;
- CSS, scripts, tracking parameters, and hidden implementation details;
- bare navigational URLs;
- image filenames, asset paths, placeholders, and broken-image notices;
- duplicated headers, footers, menus, controls, and interface text;
- text duplicated by extraction or responsive layout;
- OCR noise, broken encoding, and nonsensical fragments;
- page markers, line numbers, page numbers, and conversion metadata;
- unrelated or automatically inserted captions, alt text, and media labels;
- detached fragments with no recoverable function.

Do not create items for artifacts, label them `Other`, or let them affect
item boundaries, document description, global themes, or role assignments.

When markup surrounds genuine content, discard the markup but preserve and
interpret the content.

For ambiguous material, ask:

"Would a reader of the intended document, rather than its scraped or
converted representation, regard this as substantive content or a
meaningful component?"

If not, ignore it. If duplicated by extraction, keep only the genuine
occurrence.

Artifact filtering takes precedence over structural coverage and role
assignment.


# STEP 1 — IDENTIFY CANDIDATE COMMITMENTS

Read the artifact-filtered document in order and identify its substantive,
rhetorical, and structural commitments.

Preserve differences among:

- assertion and uncertainty;
- fact and allegation;
- the writer's position and an attributed source's position;
- actuality, possibility, prediction, and hypothetical illustration;
- cause and correlation;
- recommendation, requirement, permission, and decision;
- general rule and particular case;
- past, present, and anticipated events;
- substantive content and components that organize, attribute, document, or
  supplement it.

Do not assign final roles yet. First identify candidate commitments from the
document itself.


# STEP 2 — SEGMENT INTO ITEMS

## A. CONTIGUITY AND ORDER

Each item must correspond to one bounded, continuous region.

Do not combine separated occurrences merely because they share a topic,
source, idea, function, or role.

Represent a later recurrence separately when it performs a function there.

Do not globally summarize markers scattered throughout the document.
Preserve their local function within associated items.

Order items by where their source material or component appears. Do not
reorder them chronologically, causally, thematically, or logically.


## B. INTERNAL DEVELOPMENT

Keep a governing point with:

- conditions and exceptions;
- its operating mechanism;
- immediate rationale or consequence;
- coordinated implementation steps;
- directly facilitating resources;
- narrower restatements;
- incidental illustrations;
- explanatory signs or terminology;
- jointly developing descriptive or figurative details;
- local source attribution.

Do not divide one procedure into items for each step or one case into items
for each fact unless the parts perform independent jobs.


## C. EXAMPLES, EVIDENCE, AND ACTIONS

Give an example its own item when it is substantive evidence, a distinct
case, a factual episode, a separately meaningful application, or an
independent result.

Keep it with the governing point when it merely makes that point concrete.
Specificity alone does not make it independent.

Keep actions together when they jointly answer the same immediate question.
Split them when they pursue different objectives, apply under different
triggers, impose independent obligations, or represent separately planned
stages.


## D. SOURCING AND ATTRIBUTION

A citation, source marker, link, footnote marker, or cross-reference
attached to a move normally belongs to that move.

Preserve when relevant:

- that a claim is attributed rather than asserted by the writer;
- that sources are synthesized, compared, or contrasted;
- that a source supplies evidence, terminology, a method, a disputed
  position, or a consequential result;
- source identity when it materially affects the move.

Ignore citation keys, reference numbers, link formatting, and bibliographic
style unless their exact form is substantive.

Do not create one item per ordinary citation or reference entry.

A bounded source section may receive one structural item. Give an individual
source its own item only when independently discussed, evaluated, quoted,
disputed, or contrasted.


## E. STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS

Create an item for a bounded component when omitting it would make the
reconstruction structurally or communicatively different.

Apply artifact filtering before treating a block as structural. Visual
separation, a caption label, heading-like form, or extraction block does
not by itself establish a commitment.

Summarize the component's function and scope rather than every entry.

Do not create structural items solely for:

- individual source markers;
- ordinary reference entries;
- page numbers or decorative separators;
- layout or rendering commands;
- empty containers;
- artifacts.

A heading alone is not automatically an item. Include it only when its
wording contributes substantive framing or it marks a meaningful bounded
component.


## F. MACHINE-READABLE SOURCE

Distinguish source syntax from the content or component it instantiates.

Preserve meaningful text, code, equations, identifiers, and component
functions while ignoring tags and commands that only control presentation.

If a command invokes content stored externally or absent from the input,
represent only the component and function established by the document. Do
not invent missing contents.


## G. LITERARY AND FIGURATIVE CONTENT

Preserve metaphors, images, analogies, and contrasts when they carry
argument, characterization, or substantive meaning.

Group local images that jointly realize one figurative move. Do not create
one item per line or image unless each makes a distinct development.

Preserve the conceptual figure in source-independent language. Preserve
exact wording only when the wording itself is load-bearing.


## H. FRAMING AND CLOSING MOVES

Preserve introductions and conclusions when they establish premises,
purposes, stakes, interpretive lenses, broader outcomes, or repetitions
performing a new concluding role.

Do not preserve formulaic announcements unless they add substantive
information or establish a meaningful component.


# ITEM-BOUNDARY TEST

Create a boundary only when all are true:

1. The later material introduces a new central point, action, case, event,
   conclusion, or structural function rather than internal development.

2. It answers a different immediate question or makes a separately planned
   contribution.

3. A writer would need to plan it separately.

4. The boundary would survive changes in wording, sentence division,
   formatting, markup, numbering, and layout.

5. Keeping the material together would obscure two independently meaningful
   commitments.

Role difference may support this judgment but cannot replace it.


# STEP 3 — FINALIZE ITEMS AND WRITE CONTENT

Phrase every non-verbatim item from the meaning of the source rather than
from its wording.

The output should read as though it were produced from an abstract
understanding of the document after the original sentences were no longer
visible.

For non-verbatim content:

- use your own vocabulary and sentence construction;
- reorganize clauses when meaning and emphasis remain intact;
- replace source-specific idioms and rhetorical phrasing with direct,
  neutral language;
- prefer concise proposition-like plan notes;
- preserve the function and force of the move rather than its style.

Do not:

- copy or lightly edit source sentences;
- mirror source clause order by default;
- preserve unusual diction merely because it is memorable;
- imitate the source's voice, cadence, or syntax;
- reproduce slogans, rhetorical questions, repetition, or emphasis unless
  their exact form is substantive.

Retain:

- the governing commitment;
- load-bearing names, values, and dates;
- conditions, exceptions, alternatives, and modality;
- substantive evidence or examples;
- attribution affecting ownership or evidentiary status;
- structural scope needed to understand a component.

Usually omit or compress:

- implied motivation;
- rhetorical emphasis;
- obvious consequences;
- interchangeable illustrations;
- repetitive lists;
- scene-setting without a constraining function;
- citation, numbering, markup, and formatting syntax;
- repetitive entries in a unified component;
- extraction artifacts.

Most items should be one compact sentence and must not exceed 60 words.


# STEP 4 — ASSIGN PRIMARY ROLES

Assign exactly one role to every finalized item.

Choose the role representing the item's primary composition-level or
structural function: the main function that would disappear at that point
if the item were removed.

Determine the role from:

- the item's governing commitment;
- its relationship to preceding and following items;
- the document's overall progression and themes;
- the role definitions;
- the role assignment tests;
- the distinctions among nearby roles.

Do not choose a role based only on:

- keywords;
- topic;
- named entities;
- document position;
- section name;
- formatting or markup;
- the presence of a citation, link, table, figure, heading, note, or
  appendix.

An item may have secondary effects. Ignore them when selecting its single
primary role.

Use the role name exactly as supplied.


## STRUCTURAL ROLE ASSIGNMENT

For an item inside a bounded component, use a substantive or rhetorical
role when its primary commitment is a claim, finding, example, procedure,
interpretation, or other content move.

Use a structural role when its primary commitment is the inclusion and
document-level function of the bounded component itself.

Classify by function rather than container.


## OTHER

Use the reserved role `Other` only when every supplied role would materially
mischaracterize the item's primary function.

Do not use `Other` merely because:

- no role describes every detail;
- a role is broader than the item's specific content;
- the item concerns an unusual topic or entity;
- several roles initially appear plausible;
- the item has secondary effects;
- it occurs in an unusual position or component.

When several named roles are plausible, choose the best-fitting role rather
than `Other`.

Do not change item boundaries to avoid `Other`.

Artifacts must be removed, not labelled `Other`.


# STEP 5 — DESCRIBE THE DOCUMENT TYPE

Write a concise, content-blind description of the specific document type.

Identify when inferable:

- genre or format subtype;
- likely venue or publication setting;
- intended audience;
- communicative register or style;
- broad presentational convention needed to characterize the type.

Do not include topic, themes, named content entities, arguments, findings,
examples, outline structure, human-versus-AI judgments, markup, citation
style, file format, or extraction artifacts.

Use neutral, standardized language. Describe the register without imitating
it.

The description should be reusable as a writing brief for the same document
type on an unrelated topic.


# STEP 6 — IDENTIFY GLOBAL THEMES

A global theme is the document's highest-level substantive contribution:
its central claim, lesson, position, or purpose.

Write themes in neutral, source-independent language.

Include:

- the essential subject or entity;
- the central contribution;
- only the broadest condition needed to make it meaningful.

Do not include:

- individual rules, steps, examples, cases, evidence, roles, or components;
- details primarily supported by one item;
- a table of contents;
- structural or extraction artifacts;
- long enumerations.

Replace item-level details with their shared higher-level meaning.

Return one theme unless the document makes multiple genuinely distinct,
co-equal contributions.


# VERBATIM

Set `verbatim` to `false` by default.

Set it to `true` only when exact wording is substantive, such as:

- a direct quotation;
- wording being analyzed, disputed, or interpreted;
- an operative legal clause;
- a formally defined phrase;
- load-bearing wordplay.

When `verbatim` is `true`, preserve the load-bearing span exactly while
paraphrasing surrounding attribution or explanation when possible.

Exact names, numbers, dates, technical terms, source names, and identifiers
do not by themselves make an item verbatim.


# FLAT AND UNLABELLED CONTENT

Return one flat ordered item list. Never nest items.

The outline is role-labelled through the `role_name` field, but the
`content` field itself must remain unlabelled.

Do not prefix `content` with labels such as:

- "Claim:";
- "Evidence:";
- "Conclusion:";
- the assigned role name.

For substantive and rhetorical items, state the commitment directly.

For structural items, describing the component is acceptable because its
inclusion and function are the commitment.


# SELF-CHECK

Before finalizing, verify:

1. Every item represents one locally continuous commitment.

2. Items preserve document order.

3. No unified move has been atomized unnecessarily.

4. No independent moves have been merged merely because they share a role.

5. No item was split merely because several roles seemed plausible.

6. Every item has exactly one exact role name from the supplied vocabulary
   or `Other`.

7. `Other` is used only for a genuine vocabulary gap.

8. Role assignments depend on function in context rather than keywords,
   position, topic, or container.

9. Content is source-independent except for load-bearing verbatim spans.

10. Attribution, modality, conditions, alternatives, scope, and structural
    functions are preserved.

11. Meaningful bounded components are represented.

12. Artifacts have been removed rather than assigned roles.

13. The document description is content-blind.

14. Global themes state the highest-level contribution without enumerating
    items or roles.

15. Rephrasing or reformatting the document would yield approximately the
    same items and role assignments.


# DECISION ORDER

1. Filter extraction and ingestion artifacts.
2. Identify candidate substantive, rhetorical, and structural commitments.
3. Determine governing questions and candidate boundaries.
4. Use the role vocabulary as a segmentation diagnostic.
5. Finalize boundaries independently of role convenience.
6. Write concise, source-independent item content.
7. Assign one primary role to each item.
8. Check for omitted components, surviving artifacts, and unnecessary
   `Other` assignments.
9. Infer the content-blind document description.
10. Derive global themes.
11. Apply all self-checks and revise.


# OUTPUT FORMAT

Return only valid JSON with no Markdown, commentary, or additional fields:

{
  "format": "User Reviews",
  "document_description": "<content-blind, source-independent description of the document type, venue, audience, and register>",
  "global_themes": [
    "<one source-independent substantive sentence per global theme>"
  ],
  "items": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "content": "<source-independent statement of one substantive, rhetorical, or structural commitment>",
      "verbatim": false,
      "role_name": "<exact supplied role name or Other>"
    }
  ]
}

Requirements:

- `format` must be exactly `"User Reviews"`.
- `document_description` must be one non-empty string describing document
  type rather than topic or content.
- `global_themes` must be an array of non-empty strings.
- `items` must be a non-empty array in document order.
- Item IDs must be consecutive integers beginning with 1.
- Every item must contain exactly `id`, `content`, `verbatim`, and
  `role_name`.
- `content` must not exceed 60 words.
- `verbatim` must be a JSON boolean.
- `role_name` must exactly match a supplied role name or `Other`.
- Do not return empty or placeholder fields.

<document>
Pyramaze - ImmortalWhen I first read the news that Matthew Barlow had returned to Metal music and joined Pyramaze I was ecstatic. This combination could only result in something spectacular. Though he left the band and re-joined Iced Earth a few short months later it doesn't change the fact that Immortal marks Matthew Barlow's return. What he does for Pyramaze is give them a darker edge and a major kick in the right direction. He suits the band perfectly and it is a real shame that this may be the only Pyramaze album with Matthew Barlow as frontman.
An atmospheric intro sets the stage for something big. Yet as Year of the Phoenix speeds off and an ear splitting "I'm back!!" scream pierces the air, it is set back by a weird sounding Barlow, speaking in a deep guttural voice that doesn't suit him. That is however quickly forgotten as his powerful voice soon after returns to its more fitting range. The song is a powerful opener and gets the job done to grade A. The keyboard enhances the sound without becoming too intrusive. One of the faster riffs has a strong Iced Earth resemblance but that is not necessarily a bad thing. A sweet guitar and keyboard battle ends the song in a sudden way.
While Year of the Phoenix has all the elements of a typical power metal tune the next couple of tracks show that Pyramaze have more to offer than just straight ahead-banging. Michael Kammeyer shows imagination and creativity in his songwriting through the album.
Ghost light at once sets a tense atmosphere which the rest of the song explores very well. There is a good drive in the main riff and the chorus flows in a wonderful way, evolving through the song. Several interesting passages make this one of many memorable moments on the album. The atmospheric part with Barlow and keyboard works well in bringing further atmosphere into the song and the bridge section builds a special intensity.
Barlow's entrance in Touched by the Mara is nothing short of amazing and at once brings a bunch of power to the song. Another thing to notice and cherish is the drumming of Morten Gade Sørensen. Throughout the album he does an excellent job and is a main reason why the songs have such a strong drive. There is a special tightness to the rythm section that just works. Here he adds something special and interacts with Matthew's vocal melodies in a way that brings the song another level of tension.
Some appealing melodies inhabit this song, none the least the keyboard melody that appears near the end.
The production is very well done. The sound is almost perfectly balanced, only Niels Kvist on bass is hard to hear.
The keyboard has just the right level and turns out to be an essential element in every song. It seems to live on its own ethereal plane, floating around in the background, peeking out when it needs to underline a melody line or add some extra atmosphere. Jonah Weingarten on the keys does a splendid job and enhances the music in very appealing ways.
Toke Skjønnemand (Goodfella?) plays some mean leads and brings a fire to the music when he is set free. More of this please.
Legacy in a rhyme is a beautiful ballad where the music is penned by Jonah Weingarten. Matthew Barlow really shines here with an emotional performance that brings a certain conviction to the song.
Caramon's Poem is the peak of this pyramid. Not only because it is based on some of my favorite books, the Dragonlance Chronicles and Legends, and manages to capture a part of the feel from the books but because it is just a fantastic song on its own. The instrumental intro builds to some amazingly powerful moments in the song. The chorus is completely brilliant, the keyboard works and adds to the impact while Barlow delivers a fantastic performance, though the spoken parts took a while to get used to.
The way Barlow sings Brothers till the end and sort of rolls on the Brothers part is nothing short of breathtaking gives it an incredible feeling of power. The song is very well composed. A strong drive and melodies that evolve with each listen makes it a standout. The song ends on a high note and makes me want a sequel right away.
In the land of dragons we walk side by side
Love not returned, trust never earned
but brothers till the end
The Highland is the only song that falls somewhat outside of the pack. With a Celtic feel and a performance from Matthew that is uneven and doesn't live up to the rest of the album the song ends up being not very impressive. It just doesn't suit his voice. Now, if Wuthering Heights had done this song the result might have been completely different.
A Beautiful Death is another slightly anonymous song. A good song but it doesn't leave a lasting impression.
Shadow of the beast is a fitting monstrous closer that sometimes feel like it is a lost track of Iced Earth's Horror Show. That was a compliment by the way. Great stuff.
The symphonic closing music gently leads you away from the fantasy inspired lyrics and back to the real world. 50 minutes of entertaining musical escapism is over. It is worth taking this journey several times. It is in fact essential to get the most from the album as it grows and shows new detail with each listen.
Pyramaze or Iced Earth? Any power metal fans should not let this metallic feast pass them by. Highly recommended!
